title: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
summary: On 30 January 1948, a little after 5 pm, Mohandas Gandhi was shot three times at point-blank range by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist, as he walked to his daily prayer meeting in the garden of Birla House, New Delhi. Godse opposed Gandhi's stance toward Muslims and Pakistan after Partition. Godse and Narayan Apte were hanged in November 1949.

uncertainty.note: Date agrees across three opened pages. Time of day is given only as "a little after 5 pm" by Live History India.

as_recorded.value: On January 30, 1948, Godse assassinated Gandhi in New Delhi

where.modern_name: Gandhi Smriti (formerly Birla House), Tees January Marg, New Delhi, India
where.historical_name: Birla House, New Delhi, Dominion of India

importance.justification: Killing of the leader of the Indian independence movement five months after independence and Partition.

audience_note: Describes the shooting of Gandhi at close range and the political violence around Partition.

related.because: Godse blamed Gandhi for conceding too much to minorities and for the violence that accompanied Partition (EBSCO).

sources.title: Birla House (Gandhi Smriti) (Wikidata Q1381516), coordinates 28.601861 N, 77.214361 E

reviewer_note: Pin is Birla House (Gandhi Smriti). Gandhi's reported last words are disputed and left out. The trial opened in May 1948 at the Red Fort and the hangings (Ambala Jail) are dated November 1949 only by month in Live History India.

beats.caption: Nathuram Godse shot Gandhi at close range as he walked to his evening prayer meeting at Birla House in New Delhi.
The murder trial opened at the Red Fort in Delhi, with Godse as main defendant.
Godse and Narayan Apte were sentenced to death and hanged at Ambala Jail.
